checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is fork digest computation consistent across all client implementations incorporating blob parameters?

reachability.notes: Fork digest determines gossip topic subscription. If clients compute different digests, they subscribe to different topics and cannot communicate, causing a network partition. P2P peers can exploit this by targeting clients with known misimplementations.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all client implementations of compute_fork_digest function. 2. Verify that get_blob_parameters(epoch) is correctly called and blob parameters are incorporated into the digest. 3. Cross-test multiple client implementations with identical (epoch, genesis_validators_root) inputs to confirm identical fork digest outputs. 4. Verify the computation follows: ForkDigest(bytes(xor(compute_fork_data_root(fork_version, genesis_validators_root), hash(uint_to_bytes(blob_params.epoch) + uint_to_bytes(blob_params.max_blobs_per_block))))[:4]). 5. Test edge cases: epoch boundaries, max_blobs_per_block changes, and genesis_validators_root variations. 6. Attempt to cause digest mismatch by fuzzing blob parameter values at epoch transitions.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030, Trust Boundary: tb-010, Source Invariant: FULU-SG003-INV-001, Source Threat: stride-008. A fork digest disagreement between client implementations would cause a complete network partition. Nodes running different implementations would be unable to gossip blocks and attestations, splitting the network into isolated groups.

checklist.title: Verify P2P Peer to Consensus Layer Data Flow: Are blob parameters correctly propagated and serialized in fork digest computation?

reachability.notes: Fork digest determines gossip topic subscription. If clients compute different digests, they subscribe to different topics and cannot communicate, causing a network partition. P2P peers can exploit this by targeting clients with known misimplementations.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace data flow from consensus layer (actor-consensus-layer) to P2P peer (actor-p2p-peer). 2. Verify get_blob_parameters returns correct (epoch, max_blobs_per_block) values at all epoch boundaries. 3. Confirm uint_to_bytes serialization is consistent (endianness, padding). 4. Verify hash function implementation matches specification. 5. Test XOR operation between compute_fork_data_root output and blob parameter hash. 6. Verify truncation to first 4 bytes is correctly applied. 7. Monitor gossip topic subscriptions during epoch transitions to detect any transient inconsistencies.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030, Covered Nodes: actor-p2p-peer, actor-consensus-layer, Primary Element: SG-003. Supporting check for boundary edge tb-010.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is fork digest truncation using exactly the first 4 bytes ([:4]) of the XOR result?

reachability.notes: Truncation direction is a subtle implementation detail that could easily differ between big-endian and little-endian interpretations.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate all implementations of compute_fork_digest or equivalent fork digest computation functions. 2. Verify that the truncation operation takes exactly the first 4 bytes (indices 0-3, i.e., [:4]) of the XOR result, NOT the last 4 bytes or any middle subset. 3. Test with known input values and compare against reference implementations from other consensus clients. 4. Check for any endianness assumptions in the truncation logic - ensure big-endian vs little-endian handling is consistent with specification. 5. Verify cross-client compatibility by computing fork digests with identical inputs across multiple client implementations. 6. Review any byte manipulation utilities used in the truncation to ensure they correctly handle the [:4] slice operation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0031, Source Invariant: FULU-SG003-INV-002, Trust Boundary: tb-010, Primary Element: SG-003. Critical severity because using wrong byte ordering for truncation would produce different fork digests, causing network partitions and consensus failures. Requires cross-client verification for domain separation correctness.

checklist.title: Verify Consensus Layer Actor Handles Fork Digest Domain Separation Correctly

reachability.notes: Truncation direction is a subtle implementation detail that could easily differ between big-endian and little-endian interpretations.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the actor-consensus-layer component's usage of fork digests for domain separation. 2. Verify that the 4-byte truncated fork digest is used consistently in all message signing and verification operations. 3. Check that domain separation prevents cross-fork message replay attacks. 4. Test that messages signed with one fork digest are rejected when verified against a different fork digest. 5. Ensure the truncated digest uniquely identifies the fork within the expected collision resistance bounds.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0031, Supporting node check for actor-consensus-layer. Ensures internal logic properly leverages the boundary-defined fork digest truncation for secure domain separation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do different blob parameter configurations (epoch, max_blobs_per_block) produce different fork digests with high probability?

reachability.notes: If different blob configs produce the same digest, a peer could send blocks valid under one config on a topic expecting another config, causing peers to process blocks with wrong blob limits.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the fork digest computation function that incorporates blob parameters (epoch, max_blobs_per_block). 2. Review the XOR operation with blob parameter hash to ensure it properly differentiates configurations. 3. Generate test cases with varying blob parameter combinations and compute their fork digests. 4. Verify that all distinct configurations produce distinct 4-byte fork digests across a representative sample. 5. Analyze collision probability - confirm it approaches theoretical 1/2^32 for random inputs. 6. Check gossip topic subscription logic to verify topics are derived from fork digests correctly. 7. Attempt to craft two configurations with the same fork digest and verify system behavior (should be computationally infeasible). 8. Verify that blocks gossiped on one topic are rejected if they contain blob counts exceeding that topic's expected max_blobs_per_block.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0032, Trust Boundary: tb-010, Invariant: FULU-SG003-INV-003, Threat: stride-020. If two different blob configurations collide to the same 4-byte fork digest, blocks from one epoch could be gossiped on another epoch's topic, causing validation confusion. The probability of accidental collision is low (1/2^32).

checklist.title: Verify P2P Peer Message Handling: Are incoming blocks validated against the expected blob configuration for the gossip topic?

reachability.notes: If different blob configs produce the same digest, a peer could send blocks valid under one config on a topic expecting another config, causing peers to process blocks with wrong blob limits.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify message handlers for incoming blocks on P2P gossip topics. 2. Verify that the handler extracts and validates the fork digest from the topic name. 3. Confirm that the expected blob parameters (max_blobs_per_block) are derived from the fork digest. 4. Test rejection behavior when a block contains more blobs than the topic's expected limit. 5. Test rejection behavior when a block from a different epoch/configuration arrives on the wrong topic. 6. Verify that validation occurs before any state changes or block processing. 7. Check for timing-based attacks where epoch transitions could create windows of confusion.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0032, Supporting check for actor-p2p-peer node coverage.

checklist.title: Verify Consensus Layer Fork Digest Derivation: Is the blob parameter hash correctly incorporated into fork digest computation ensuring configuration separation?

reachability.notes: If different blob configs produce the same digest, a peer could send blocks valid under one config on a topic expecting another config, causing peers to process blocks with wrong blob limits.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the consensus layer code that computes fork digests. 2. Verify that blob parameters (epoch, max_blobs_per_block) are included in the hash input. 3. Confirm the XOR operation is applied correctly and cannot be bypassed. 4. Review for any edge cases where blob parameters might be zero or default values. 5. Test fork digest computation at epoch boundaries to ensure correct parameter selection. 6. Verify consistency between the fork digest used for topic subscription and the one used for message validation. 7. Confirm that two epochs with different blob limits MUST result in different gossip topic subscriptions.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0032, Supporting check for actor-consensus-layer node coverage.
